message.content:
Second independent check. Is this M12 code-review finding a REAL, actionable bug/issue that should be fixed before merge? Read the code yourself. Be skeptical — confirm only if you can point to the concrete problem in the diff.

Lens: reuse
File: messages/en.json (account.removeFavorite, account.cancelConfirm, account.settingsHeading)
Title: Three dead message keys added but never referenced
Detail: This diff adds `account.removeFavorite` ("Remove {name} from favorites"), `account.cancelConfirm` ("Cancel this booking?"), and `account.settingsHeading` ("Payment & settings") to the catalog, but grep across app/ and components/ shows zero usages of any of them. `account.removeFavorite` is also a duplicate of `favorite.remove` ("Remove {name} from favorites"), which is the key actually used by FavoriteButton. `account.settingsHeading` duplicates the used `account.settingsTitle`. `account.cancelConfirm` was evidently authored for a cancel confirmation that was never wired up (see related finding).

This confirms the finding precisely.

The three keys in question have zero references via the `t()` accessor:
- `account.removeFavorite` — 0 usages. The `removeFavorite` grep hits are all a server-action function of the same name (unrelated). The live key for the favorite button label is `favorite.remove` (used in `FavoriteButton.tsx:54`), with identical text "Remove {name} from favorites" — confirming the duplication claim.
- `account.cancelConfirm` — 0 usages. `UpcomingBookings.tsx` uses `account.cancel`, `account.cancelledRefund`, `account.cancelledCharged`, but never `cancelConfirm`. No confirmation dialog is wired up.
- `account.settingsHeading` — 0 usages. The live key is `account.settingsTitle` (used in `settings/page.tsx:11,28`), with identical text "Payment & settings" — confirming the duplication claim.

Since keys are accessed only as full dotted string literals (no dynamic key construction in `lib/i18n.ts`), a literal grep is the authoritative test, and all three come up empty.

That said, on severity: these are unused strings in a JSON catalog, not a functional bug. They cause no runtime error, no type error, and no incorrect behavior. The accuracy of the finding is solid; whether it "should be fixed before merge" is a judgment call about dead-code hygiene. The finding is real and actionable (delete the three keys), even if low severity.

I've verified the M12 finding. It is real and actionable, though low severity.

All three keys (`account.removeFavorite`, `account.cancelConfirm`, `account.settingsHeading`) added in the M12 diff to `messages/en.json` have zero references via the `t()` accessor. Since `lib/i18n.ts` resolves keys only from full dotted string literals (no dynamic key construction), a literal grep is authoritative, and all three come up empty. Two are exact-text duplicates of keys that ARE in use (`favorite.remove` and `account.settingsTitle` respectively). The `removeFavorite` grep hits are a red herring — they reference a same-named server-action function, not the message key.

The fix is straightforward (delete the three dead keys). It is dead-catalog hygiene rather than a functional bug, so no runtime or type error results from leaving them in.
